title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 35-37). Gamma is a subgroup of Autext of the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus three points, satisfying 'congruence conditions'; it plays the role of a Grothendieck-Teichmueller-type group. M_{0,3} is an extension of Gamma by the profinite modular-type group T^_{0,3}, which is isomorphic to SL(2,Z)^+. The previous page built two maps on M_{0,3}: phi' to GP(1,Z^) = PGL(2,Z^), and the cyclotomic character chi to Z^*. The congruence conditions make the combined map u -> (phi'(u), chi(u)) factor as (42), psi': M_{0,3} -> GL(2,Z^)/_2Z^*.

The notation _2Z^* means the 2-torsion of Z^*, i.e. the square roots of 1 in Z^* = prod_p Z_p^*. This is prod_p {+-1} = (Z/2)^P. With that reading, (43) is the injection GL(2,Z^)/mu_2 -> PGL(2,Z^) x Z^*, u -> (class mod scalars, det u). The kernel is scalars lambda with lambda^2 = 1, which have already been divided out, so the map is injective.

GL(2,Z^)' := GL(2,Z^)/{+-1} surjects onto GL(2,Z^)/mu_2(Z^) (44). The kernel is mu_2(Z^)/{+-1} = (Z/2)^P/diagonal = nu (45). This is central.

Pulling (44) back along psi' gives a central extension 1 -> nu -> M~_{0,3} -> M_{0,3} -> 1 (46). Lifting psi' to M_{0,3} -> GL(2,Z^)' (47) is equivalent to splitting (46).

The question posed is whether such a lift can be made canonical using only Gamma inside Autext(pi^_{0,3}). The next page continues:
- Over T^_{0,3} the lift is known: SL(2,Z)^ -> SL(2,Z^)/+-1.
- The splittings form a torsor under Hom(M_{0,3}, nu), which shrinks to Ker(Hom(M,nu) -> Hom(T,nu)) = Hom(Gamma, nu).
- If Gamma^ab = Z^* via chi, this becomes Hom(Z^*/Z^*2, nu), which he notes is 'big'.

Meaning: nu measures independent sign choices at each prime, modulo a global sign. A lift is a prime-by-prime coherent choice of quadratic twist for the 2-dimensional 'Tate-module' representation attached to the Legendre-type situation. For G_Q, the Tate module of the Legendre curve y^2 = x(x-1)(x-lambda) gives such a lift. The problem is to find the analogue for an abstract Gamma (e.g. GT).
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The kernel computation in (45) is right: mu_2(Z^) = prod_p {+-1}, including p = 2, since Z_2^* has torsion {+-1}. Quotienting by the global +-1 gives (Z/2)^P/diag. Centrality of nu, and the equivalence 'lift of (42) <=> splitting of the pulled-back extension', are both correct.
Minor: the homomorphism named in the sentence before (46) should be psi' (42), as on the previous page, not phi' (40). This is a notation slip, or a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Injection GL(2,Z^)/mu_2(Z^) -> PGL(2,Z^) x Z^* via (projective class, det)
ideas.modern_name: elementary structure of GL_2 over the profinite integers

ideas.what: Kernel of GL(2,Z^)/+-1 -> GL(2,Z^)/mu_2 is (Z/2)^P/diag; obstruction to a lift is the central extension pulled back along psi'
ideas.modern_name: central extension / quadratic-twist ambiguity of a projective Galois-type representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (cf. lifting projective Galois representations, Tate, Serre)

ideas.what: Asking whether a GT-like group Gamma acting on pi^_{0,3} canonically yields a lift to GL(2,Z^)/+-1, extending the known map on the profinite modular group, i.e. a GT-analogue of the Tate-module representation of the universal or Legendre elliptic curve
ideas.modern_name: GT actions on profinite SL2(Z)/B3 and genus-one GT; Galois action on pi_1(M_{1,1}) with its GL2(Z^) representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps, Hain-Matsumoto, Enriquez (genus-one GT)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses GT-type actions on Teichmueller towers generally. This specific GL2 lifting question is not there to my knowledge.

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates a precise obstruction: a central extension of M_{0,3} by (Z/2)^P/diag. He asks whether a GT-type group Gamma canonically determines a lift to GL(2,Z^)/+-1, a 'Tate-module of the Legendre curve' for Gamma. He notes the residual indeterminacy Hom(Gamma, nu), which reduces to Hom(Z^*/Z^*2, nu) if Gamma^ab = Z^*, is large. The thread breaks off unresolved here.
missed.quote: La question à élucider à présent : est-il possible d'expliciter un tel relèvement canonique de (42), ou scindage de (46), en termes de la seule donnée de Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It asks whether GT (not only G_Q) carries a canonical 2-dimensional profinite representation compatible with its action on SL2(Z)^. This connects to genus-one GT (Enriquez, Nakamura) and Hain-Matsumoto. The prime-by-prime quadratic-twist formulation is a concrete test question I have not seen stated in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are routine. The interest is in the explicit formulation of a canonical GL2(Z^)-lift problem for an abstract GT-type group, with the obstruction identified as (Z/2)^P/diag. Related questions were studied later (GT on SL2(Z)^, genus-one GT, Hain-Matsumoto), so this is a notable but not startling unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'L'hom. canonique φ' (42)': the image and the previous page indicate psi' (the map labelled (42)).
'/_2 Ẑ^*' should be read as quotient by the 2-torsion subgroup _2Ẑ^* = mu_2(Ẑ), not by squares.
'GP(1,Ẑ)' denotes PGL(2,Ẑ), the projective group of P^1 (the previous page's 'Gl(1,Ẑ)[?]' is likely GP(1,Ẑ) too).
Line 'dont le noyau est donné' is followed by (45) ν = (Z/2Z)^P/diag with P = ensemble des nombres premiers: correct.
